samples.text: The valuation is running on a workaround, and its basis is explicit. The position in force is: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That override rests on the working diagnosis, which reads: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. In effect, the faulty entries were replaced by hand for this run so that the period valuation could proceed while the register itself stays uncorrected. Its accuracy depends entirely on the care of the engineers who applied it. This is a holding arrangement. It is not a fix, and it has not been exercised beyond the current period. Two points bear on whether to wait for a permanent correction. First, the override covers this period only; the next run will read the same uncorrected register and can fail in the same way. Second, a mapping applied by hand carries its own risk of error, so outputs produced under it deserve a check before anything final relies on them. Waiting is reasonable for

The established cause of the valuation failure is this: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. The review classifies the root cause as a control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. That classification matters more than the stale entry itself, because a table with nobody accountable for it and no review step will drift again whenever an agency code changes on one side of the estate. The first working theory pointed somewhere else entirely. It was initially recorded as: overnight ERP outage. That theory did not survive the evidence, and a single test ruled it out: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window.
